title: KidsAbility playground funding and nuisance by-law updates
subtitle: Parks by-law ax-throwing ban, student housing report, Dietz Avenue tower public meeting, basic income notice of motion, strong mayor powers
overview: Council approved $25,000 from its Community Priority and Contingency Reserve toward KidsAbility's new fully accessible playground and authorized a land use agreement with the organization for 2023 to 2043 {{vote:m7}}. It also amended the Public Nuisance By-law and the related administrative penalties by-law, including a standing definition for homecoming and a new nuisance party provision {{vote:m8}}, and amended the Parks By-law {{vote:m6}}. Funding was released for signs and pavement markings and for intersection collision review work {{vote:m5}}.

Council endorsed the Town and Gown Committee's student accommodation report and its next steps {{vote:m10}}. It received an update on the Beechwood West II special service area levy vote as information {{vote:m9}}. Staff expect to report back on the vote result on October 16.

Council also held an informal public meeting on a proposed 13-storey rental apartment building on Dietz Avenue North. No decision was made, and staff will report back at a later date. A notice of motion on a guaranteed livable basic income was tabled for September 18. The mayor stated that the strong mayor powers will not be used. The formal public meeting on a Hemlock Street application was deferred.

decisions.item: KidsAbility playground and land use agreement
decisions.detail: Council approved $25,000 from the Community Priority and Contingency Reserve for KidsAbility's accessible playground and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign a 2023 to 2043 land use agreement.
Council approved amendments to the Public Nuisance By-law and the General Administrative Penalties By-law, including a nuisance party definition and a defined roofing activity.
Council approved amendments to the Parks By-law, including specifically prohibiting ax throwing in parks.

decisions.item: Signs, pavement markings and collision review funding
decisions.detail: Council released $263,000 for signs and pavement marking and $105,000 for intersection collision review and implementation from the 2023 capital budget.

decisions.item: Town and Gown student accommodation report
decisions.detail: Council endorsed report CTTEE2023-002 and supported the committee's planned next steps on student housing.

decisions.item: Beechwood West II levy vote update
decisions.detail: Council received report CORP2023-041 on the special service area levy vote as information.

debate: On the Town and Gown report, one councillor asked what the high student satisfaction figure really means when many students reported trade-offs on food and utilities. The presenter said satisfied was not defined and may reflect gratitude for having housing, and that the working group will look deeper.

Councillors also noted that international students were under-represented among survey respondents and may be less likely to come forward. Another suggested using rental housing index data and creating a one-stop information resource for tenants. One councillor asked whether institutions are doing enough on-campus building, and the presenter said all parties have a role.

At the Dietz Avenue meeting, residents of the neighbouring seniors building and nearby homes raised concerns about shadows, wind, privacy, parking, traffic, construction dust and loss of sunlight. One resident said the reports contained errors and did not account for the nearby approved development.

The applicant's representative said the building is purpose-built rental with larger family-sized units, 10 percent affordable units tied to its CMHC financing, and a parking rate supported by its study. A supporter pointed to low vacancy rates and the need for housing. Council asked about affordability, parking and shadow studies, and the applicant offered to hold a neighbourhood meeting.

On the Public Nuisance By-law, a councillor asked whether the nuisance party provision applies year-round. Staff said it could apply at any time if clear behaviours meeting the definition were present.
